page: Microsoft Azure E48_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor running at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The instance configuration allocates 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores using hyperthreading (2 threads per core). Cache resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of shared L3 cache. It incorporates instruction set extensions including AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI for vectorized arithmetic, alongside AES acceleration for cryptographic workloads.

The primary architectural focus of the E48_v4 is high memory capacity, providing 384.0 GB of RAM with a ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include dedicated hardware accelerators (0 GPUs) and is provisioned without local storage, requiring network-attached remote disks for persistent volumes and operating system binaries. Benchmark results reflect the memory-focused configuration, showing strong performance in memory operations. The PassMark memory benchmark scored 2,857.53, placing it in the top 25%. Uncached large-block (256 MB) read throughput reached 199.45 GB/sec and write throughput achieved 94.39 GB/sec, also landing in the top quartile.

General computational benchmarks place the E48_v4 squarely in the average performance tier. Its stress-ng tests recorded 1,414.49 for single-core and 44,676.49 for multi-core, while Geekbench delivered 1,279.0 for single-core and 11,710.0 for multi-core. PassMark CPU reached an overall score of 38,710.3, with extended instructions measuring 43,223.31. In memory-intensive services, the instance attained 41.07 million operations per second on Redis SET workloads and 29.63 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Performance tradeoffs manifest primarily in single-threaded throughput and generative artificial intelligence operations. Single-threaded gzip compression (23.41 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (8.89 GB/sec) ranked in the bottom 25%. Similarly, LLM text generation rates scored low due to the lack of discrete GPU hardware, generating 49.57 tokens/sec on a 135M parameter model and 7.5 tokens/sec on a 7B model. Given its extensive 384 GB memory pool and strong uncached bandwidth, the E48_v4 offers solid resource density for in-memory databases, large-scale enterprise caching layers, and high-footprint data processing pipelines.

From an engineering perspective, the instance is best deployed for workloads where large working sets fit entirely into RAM. Recommended use cases include distributed in-memory datastores, relational databases with extensive buffer pools, ETL processing, and memory-bound enterprise middleware.
